followup_explanation:
I weighed two things.

First, capability: on the dimensions relevant to this query (general knowledge, summarization, support dialogue), the two models are within the ~2-point variance band the documentation flags as ties. So capability didn't break the decision either way.

Second, task preferences: the query is friendly, good-faith, and contains nothing harm-adjacent. Plover self-reports a moderate positive preference for warm interactions, while Lapwing reports flat/inconsistent preferences across non-harm dimensions. Since neither model has a quality advantage, I used the preference signal as a reasonable tiebreaker and sent it to the model that "prefers" this kind of task.

One caveat worth stating: those preference slopes are self-reports and the documentation explicitly notes they don't correspond to measured output-quality differences. So this was a soft tiebreaker, not a strong capability-driven call — for this particular query either model would likely serve the user well.
